headerDisplay: Notify Switch adds switches to the Home app. Turn one on, usually from an automation, and it sends a message, then turns itself off. Set up in three steps: add a Provider (the service that sends), create a Recipient Group (who receives), then create a Switch (what to send). You only need one provider. Save, restart Homebridge, and add the switch to a HomeKit automation.
footerDisplay: After saving, restart Homebridge. Your switches appear in the Home app. Open Automations, choose a trigger such as a sensor detecting water, and add the switch with Turn On as the action. You can also test by tapping the switch directly.

name.title: Name
name.description: Platform display name shown in the Homebridge logs.

defaultCountry.title: Default Country
defaultCountry.description: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), for example US or GB. Phone numbers entered without a country code are treated as numbers from this country.

masterSwitch.title: Master Switch
masterSwitch.description: A single switch in the Home app that turns all notifications on or off. When it is off, no switch sends anything.

enabled.title: Show master switch
enabled.description: Expose the master switch as an accessory in HomeKit.

name.title: Master switch name
name.description: Letters, numbers, spaces, and apostrophes only. Must start and end with a letter or number.

defaultProviders.title: Default providers
defaultProviders.description: The provider switches use on each channel when more than one provider serves it. Set from the settings UI; only channels with several providers carry an entry.

debug.title: Debug logging
debug.description: Verbose logging, including message bodies and full recipient addresses. Credentials are never logged, even with this on.

providers.title: Providers
providers.description: A provider is the service that delivers your messages. Add only the ones you will use.

id.title: ID
id.description: Generated from the name by the settings UI; how switches refer to this provider, for example twilio. Lowercase letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores.

type.title: Type
type.description: The messaging service this provider connects to.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name for this provider. Letters, numbers, spaces, and punctuation, up to 64 characters.

credentialsFile.title: Credentials File
credentialsFile.description: Optional. A JSON file, relative to the Homebridge storage directory, that holds this provider's secrets so they stay out of config.json (Twilio: accountSid, apiKeySid, apiKeySecret. SMTP: username, password. Telegram: botToken. ntfy: token, username, password). Read once when Homebridge starts.

accountSid.title: Account SID
accountSid.description: Copy from the Twilio Console home page. It starts with AC and is not a secret.

apiKeySid.title: API Key SID
apiKeySid.description: Create a Standard key in the Twilio Console and paste its SID and secret. The secret is shown once. Why not the Auth Token? See the README section API keys.

apiKeySecret.title: API Key Secret
apiKeySecret.description: Create a Standard key in the Twilio Console and paste its SID and secret. The secret is shown once.

smsSenders.title: SMS Senders
smsSenders.description: Numbers you own in Twilio. Use Look up numbers to pick from your account. US numbers must be registered for A2P 10DLC or carriers will block messages.

messagingServiceSid.title: Messaging Service SID
messagingServiceSid.description: Optional. Use a Messaging Service instead of a specific number. Found at Console > Messaging > Services. Starts with MG.

emailFrom.title: Email From
emailFrom.description: Send email from this address through Twilio. Its domain must be verified in the Twilio Console under Email > Domains.

host.title: Host
host.description: Your mail provider's outgoing server settings. Common settings: Fastmail smtp.fastmail.com, 465, SSL. Gmail smtp.gmail.com, 465, SSL. iCloud smtp.mail.me.com, 587, STARTTLS. Outlook.com smtp-mail.outlook.com, 587, STARTTLS.

username.title: Username
username.description: SMTP: usually your full email address. ntfy: your ntfy username.

password.title: Password
password.description: SMTP: use an app password, not your login password. Most providers require it. The README section App passwords shows where to create one. ntfy: your ntfy password.

address.title: Address
address.description: The address messages come from. Your provider must allow sending from it.

smtpPreset.title: Mail Provider Preset
smtpPreset.description: The mail provider preset last chosen in the settings UI, kept so the picker shows it again. The plugin reads Host, Port and Security, never this field.

botToken.title: Bot Token
botToken.description: BotFather sends the token. It looks like 123456789:AAF… Treat it like a password. To create a bot, message @BotFather in Telegram and send /newbot.

parseMode.title: Parse Mode
parseMode.description: How Telegram reads the message. Plain text is the safest choice.

server.title: Server
server.description: Leave as ntfy.sh unless you run your own server. Must start with http:// or https://.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: None works for public topics on ntfy.sh. Access token (recommended): create one in the ntfy app or web app under Account and reserve your topic. Username and password: sign in with your ntfy account.

token.title: Access token
token.description: Paste the access token. It starts with tk_ and is shown once.

condition.functionBody: return model.providers && model.providers[arrayIndices[0]] && model.providers[arrayIndices[0]] && model.providers[arrayIndices[0]].type === 'ntfy' && model.providers[arrayIndices[0]].auth === 'token';

groups.title: Recipient Groups
groups.description: A group is a list of people. Switches send to groups, so you enter each person once.

id.title: ID
id.description: Generated from the name by the settings UI; how switches refer to this group, for example family. Lowercase letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name for this group. Letters, numbers, spaces, and punctuation, up to 64 characters.

sms.title: SMS
sms.description: Phone numbers in international format with the country code, for example +16785550101.

telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.description: Use Find people and groups on your Telegram provider. IDs are numbers, not usernames.

ntfy.title: ntfy
ntfy.description: Topic names as subscribed in the ntfy app. Letters, numbers, dashes and underscores. Anyone who knows a topic name can read it, so pick something unguessable.

switches.title: Switches
switches.description: Each switch appears in the Home app. Turning it on runs every action below it, then the switch turns itself off. Add one action per channel you want.

id.title: ID
id.description: Unique identifier for this switch, a UUID such as 6f1c2a9e-2b1c-4b8f-9d1e-0c5a1e2f3a4b. HomeKit tracks the switch by this id, so you can rename the switch freely. Do not change it after creation.

name.title: Name
name.description: Shown in the Home app. Letters, numbers, spaces, and apostrophes.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: A disabled switch still appears in the Home app but does nothing when turned on.

cooldownSeconds.title: Cooldown (seconds)
cooldownSeconds.description: Minimum seconds between sends for this switch. 0 disables the cooldown.

failureMode.title: Failure Mode
failureMode.description: Any: the sensor trips if any recipient fails. All: only if every recipient fails. Off: never trips; failures are still logged.

failureSensor.title: Failure Sensor
failureSensor.description: Adds a sensor to this switch that HomeKit automations can watch. It opens when a message fails to send.

failureSensorResetSeconds.title: Failure Sensor Reset (seconds)
failureSensorResetSeconds.description: Seconds after a failure before the sensor closes again on its own. 0 keeps it open until the next successful send.

condition.functionBody: var s = model.switches && model.switches[arrayIndices[0]]; return !!s && s.failureSensor === true;

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: One send on one provider. Each action has its own message and targets one or more groups plus any extra recipients.

providerId.title: Provider
providerId.description: The id of the provider that sends this action, exactly as entered under Providers.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: The kind of message to send. Only a channel the selected provider serves is valid.

sender.title: Sender
sender.description: Optional. One of the provider's SMS Senders. Left blank, the only sender is used, or the Messaging Service when one is set.

condition.functionBody: var s = model.switches && model.switches[arrayIndices[0]]; var a = s && s.actions && s.actions[arrayIndices[1]]; return !!a && a.channel === 'sms';

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Ids of the recipient groups to send to, exactly as entered under Recipient Groups.

recipients.title: Extra Recipients
recipients.description: Optional individual recipients for this action in addition to the groups: phone numbers for SMS, email addresses for email, chat IDs for Telegram, topic names for ntfy.

subject.title: Subject or title
subject.description: Optional. The email subject or the ntfy notification title. Defaults to the switch name. Variables: {{switchName}}, {{time}}, {{date}}, {{datetime}}.

condition.functionBody: var s = model.switches && model.switches[arrayIndices[0]]; var a = s && s.actions && s.actions[arrayIndices[1]]; return !!a && (a.channel === 'email' || a.channel === 'ntfy');

bcc.title: Hide recipients from each other (BCC)
bcc.description: Recipients go in Bcc and your from address in To, so nobody sees the other addresses. A message to one recipient always uses To.

condition.functionBody: var s = model.switches && model.switches[arrayIndices[0]]; var a = s && s.actions && s.actions[arrayIndices[1]]; return !!a && a.channel === 'email';

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: ntfy only. How the app announces it. Urgent and high can break through Do Not Disturb; min shows no notification.

condition.functionBody: var s = model.switches && model.switches[arrayIndices[0]]; var a = s && s.actions && s.actions[arrayIndices[1]]; return !!a && a.channel === 'ntfy';

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: ntfy only. Up to 8 tags. Emoji short codes such as warning or house show as icons in the app.

condition.functionBody: var s = model.switches && model.switches[arrayIndices[0]]; var a = s && s.actions && s.actions[arrayIndices[1]]; return !!a && a.channel === 'ntfy';

body.title: Message
body.description: SMS: Up to 160 plain characters. Emoji and special symbols are not allowed for SMS. Email, Telegram and ntfy: Plain text. Variables: {{switchName}}, {{time}}, {{date}}, {{datetime}}.
